title: Imaging and downlink
summary: A normal working day: take images of the Earth and bring the data down to the ground.
goals: Point the payload at the Earth (NADIR)
Manage the data budget: collection vs downlink
Use stored commands for work outside contact
prerequisites: Low power: a solar panel has failed
situation: The satellite is in sun-safe mode, approaching Baku. Your task: collect at least 100 MB of images and deliver 50 MB to the ground. The camera drains the battery, so do not leave it on forever.

steps.hint: The pass timer shows the next AOS.

steps.text: Point the camera at the Earth: ADCS MODE NADIR.
steps.hint: The star tracker gives the best attitude knowledge for pointing.

steps.text: Switch the camera on: pl.main ON.
steps.hint: It only records over the sunlit Earth with good pointing.
'Data collected' in the Computer group. Stored data also drops while a pass downlinks it. Tip: OBSW SCHEDULE_IN 900 pl.main OFF switches the camera off later even without contact.
Data only flows during passes, through the S-band radio.

failText: The battery fell below 20%: imaging cost too much power.
successText: Data delivered. Data budget = what you can collect vs what the passes can bring down.
